On the interpretation of His words, "The revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful" (36:5):

The readers differed over the recitation of His words, "The revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful." The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra recited it as "tanzīlu al-ʿazīzi" with "tanzīl" in the nominative (rafʿ). The nominative can be justified in two ways. The first is to take it as the predicate (khabar), so the meaning of the sentence is: "It is the revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful." The second is to take it as the subject (mubtadaʾ), so the meaning of the sentence becomes: "You are indeed among the messengers; this is the revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful."

The majority of the readers of Kufa and some of the people of Syria recited it as "tanzīla al-ʿazīzi" with "tanzīl" in the accusative (naṣb), as a verbal noun (maṣdar) following His words, "Indeed you are among the messengers," because the sending (irsāl) is only by means of the revelation (tanzīl). It is as if it were said: "Surely you are one sent with the revelation of the Mighty, the Merciful, in truth."

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations among the readers of the cities, close in meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the sentence is: "Indeed you are among the messengers, O Muhammad, [sent by] the sending of the Lord, the Mighty in His vengeance upon those who disbelieve in Him, the Merciful toward whoever repents to Him and turns back from his disbelief and transgression, so that He does not punish him for his past sin after his repentance."

The interpretation of His words, "So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, and so they are heedless" (36:6), has been disputed among the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Some said: its meaning is: so that you may warn a people with what Allah warned their forefathers before them.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, regarding this verse, "So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned," he said: "They were warned."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned [i.e., whose forefathers were not warned].

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "So that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned," some said: so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned by the warning of the people before them. And some said: so that you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, i.e., this nation had no warner come to them until Muhammad (ﷺ) came to them.

The grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) differed over the meaning of the "ma" (what/that) in His words, "...what their forefathers were not warned," when the meaning of the statement is directed to the claim that their forefathers had indeed been warned, and it is not intended as a negation. Some grammarians of Basra said: the meaning of that, if it is intended other than as negation, is: so that you may warn them with what their forefathers were warned, "so they are heedless." And he said: the entry of the "fa" (so) in this sense is not permissible, and Allah knows best. He said: and it is better understood as negation, so the meaning of the statement becomes: you are indeed among the messengers to a people whose forefathers were not warned, because they were in a period of interruption (fatrah).

Some grammarians of Kufa said: if "ma" is not intended as negation, then the meaning of the statement is: so that you may warn them with what their forefathers were warned, so the preposition "bi" (with) is dropped, and "ma" is in the accusative position. "So they are heedless" means: they are heedless of what Allah will do to His enemies, the polytheists who associate others with Him, by way of bringing down His vengeance and His might upon them.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up (with their heads raised).﴾ [36:8] ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them, so they do not see.﴾ [36:9]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, We have made the right hands of these disbelievers chained to their necks with shackles, so that they are not extended toward any of the goods. It is reported that in the reading of ʿAbdullah (Ibn Masʿud) it is: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their right hands, and they reach to the chins﴾. His words ﴿and they reach to the chins﴾ mean: so their right hands are gathered with the shackles to their necks. The right hands are thus referred to by implication (kināya), and they are not mentioned explicitly because the listeners know the meaning of the speech. Since shackles on the necks cannot exist without the hands of the shackled being gathered to them, mention of the shackles being on the necks suffices in place of mention of the hands, as the poet said:

*"I do not know, when I set my face / desiring good, which of the two will befall me;*
*Is it the good that I seek, / or the evil that does not leave me alone?"* [[The two verses are in the meter al-Wafir and belong to Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi. They were previously cited (14:157) at the words of the Exalted, ﴿garments that protect you from the war﴾, in Surat al-Nahl. They are cited here to show that his words "desiring good, which of them will befall me" mean: which of good and evil will befall me. He mentioned only the good and left out the evil, since it was known from the context, as in the words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks﴾, where the right hands are not mentioned because the right hands are only in the shackles together with the necks. Thus the shackles suffice in place of mention of the right hands. Al-Farra said in Maʿani al-Qur'an (folio 267): His words ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins﴾: he refers to "they" (hiya) by implication, and it is for the right hands, though not mentioned. This is because the shackle is only on the right hand, and the neck gathers the right hand and the neck, so mention of one suffices for the other. Similar is the poet's saying: "I do not know..." the two verses. He left out the evil and mentioned only the good, because evil is mentioned together with good. In the reading of ʿAbdullah it is: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their right hands, and they reach to the chins﴾, so mention of "the necks" is dropped in the reading of ʿAbdullah, and "the necks" suffices for "the right hands" in the common reading. Al-Dhaqan: the lower part of the two jaws.]]

Thus evil is referred to by implication, and only the good is mentioned, so that the hearer knows the meaning of the speaker, since evil is commonly mentioned together with good. Al-Adhqan is the plural of dhaqan, and al-dhaqan is the meeting place of the two jaws (lihyayn).

* *

His words ﴿so they are held up﴾

Al-muqmah is the one who is made to lower his head (al-muqnaʿ), which means that he lowers his chin until it reaches his chest, and then raises his head, according to the view of some scholars of Arabic speech from Basra; and according to some Kufans, it means one who lowers his gaze after raising his head.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his words ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up﴾, he said: It is like God's words ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾, meaning that their hands are bound to their necks, so they cannot extend them toward good.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, who said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, who said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿so they are held up﴾, he said: raising their heads, with their hands placed over their mouths.

• Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up﴾: that is, they are shackled away from every good.

* *

His words ﴿And We have put a barrier before them﴾

The Exalted says: And We have put before these polytheists a barrier (sadd), which is the separating obstacle between two things. When it is pronounced with a fatha, it is the action of the children of Adam; when it is from God's action, it is with a damma. The readers of Medina, Basra and some Kufans read it with a damma. Some Meccan readers and most Kufan readers read it with a fatha, sadd, in both places. To me the damma is the more preferred of the two readings in this, although the other is also permissible and sound.

By His words ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them﴾ He means that He adorned for them the evil of their deeds, so they wander blindly, and do not see the right guidance, and do not truly awaken.

Ahl al-ta'wil said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, who said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, who said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them﴾: from the truth, so they waver.

• Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them﴾, he said: misguidance.

• Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them, so they do not see﴾: He made this a barrier between them and Islam and faith, so they cannot reach it. And he recited ﴿And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾, and he recited ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been fulfilled will not believe﴾, the whole verse, and he said: whoever God prevents cannot be able (to believe).

* *

His words ﴿so We have covered them, so they do not see﴾

He says: We covered their sight, that is, We placed a covering (ghashawah) over it; so they do not see guidance and do not benefit from it.

As:

• Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿so We have covered them, so they do not see﴾: guidance, and they do not benefit from it.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, when he swore that he would kill (the Prophet) or smash his head with a rock.

The narration regarding that:

• ʿImran ibn Musa related to me, who said: ʿAbd al-Warith ibn Saʿid related to us, who said: ʿUmarah ibn Abi Hafsa related to us, from ʿIkrimah, who said: Abu Jahl said: "If I see Muhammad, I will certainly do such-and-such," so there was revealed ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks﴾ ... to His words ﴿so they do not see﴾. He said: They used to say, "This is Muhammad," and he would say, "Where is he, where is he?" and could not see him. It has also been related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to read it: ﴿fa-aʿshaynahum﴾ with an ʿayn, meaning: We blinded them to him, because al-ʿashā is to walk at night without seeing.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up (with their heads raised).﴾ [36:8] ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them, and We have covered them, so they do not see.﴾ [36:9]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, We have made the right hands of these disbelievers chained to their necks with shackles, so that they are not extended toward any of the goods. It is reported that in the reading of ʿAbdullah (Ibn Masʿud) it is: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their right hands, and they reach to the chins﴾. His words ﴿and they reach to the chins﴾ mean: so their right hands are gathered with the shackles to their necks. The right hands are thus referred to by implication (kināya), and they are not mentioned explicitly because the listeners know the meaning of the speech. Since shackles on the necks cannot exist without the hands of the shackled being gathered to them, mention of the shackles being on the necks suffices in place of mention of the hands, as the poet said:

*"I do not know, when I set my face / desiring good, which of the two will befall me;*
*Is it the good that I seek, / or the evil that does not leave me alone?"* [[The two verses are in the meter al-Wafir and belong to Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi. They were previously cited (14:157) at the words of the Exalted, ﴿garments that protect you from the war﴾, in Surat al-Nahl. They are cited here to show that his words "desiring good, which of them will befall me" mean: which of good and evil will befall me. He mentioned only the good and left out the evil, since it was known from the context, as in the words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks﴾, where the right hands are not mentioned because the right hands are only in the shackles together with the necks. Thus the shackles suffice in place of mention of the right hands. Al-Farra said in Maʿani al-Qur'an (folio 267): His words ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins﴾: he refers to "they" (hiya) by implication, and it is for the right hands, though not mentioned. This is because the shackle is only on the right hand, and the neck gathers the right hand and the neck, so mention of one suffices for the other. Similar is the poet's saying: "I do not know..." the two verses. He left out the evil and mentioned only the good, because evil is mentioned together with good. In the reading of ʿAbdullah it is: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their right hands, and they reach to the chins﴾, so mention of "the necks" is dropped in the reading of ʿAbdullah, and "the necks" suffices for "the right hands" in the common reading. Al-Dhaqan: the lower part of the two jaws.]]

Thus evil is referred to by implication, and only the good is mentioned, so that the hearer knows the meaning of the speaker, since evil is commonly mentioned together with good. Al-Adhqan is the plural of dhaqan, and al-dhaqan is the meeting place of the two jaws (lihyayn).

* *

His words ﴿so they are held up﴾

Al-muqmah is the one who is made to lower his head (al-muqnaʿ), which means that he lowers his chin until it reaches his chest, and then raises his head, according to the view of some scholars of Arabic speech from Basra; and according to some Kufans, it means one who lowers his gaze after raising his head.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

• Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my paternal uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his words ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up﴾, he said: It is like God's words ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾, meaning that their hands are bound to their necks, so they cannot extend them toward good.

• Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, who said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, who said: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿so they are held up﴾, he said: raising their heads, with their hands placed over their mouths.

• Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, and they reach to the chins, so they are held up﴾: that is, they are shackled away from every good.

* *

His words ﴿And We have put a barrier before them﴾

The Exalted says: And We have put before these polytheists a barrier (sadd), which is the separating obstacle between two things. When it is pronounced with a fatha, it is the action of the children of Adam; when it is from God's action, it is with a damma. The readers of Medina, Basra and some Kufans read it with a damma. Some Meccan readers and most Kufan readers read it with a fatha, sadd, in both places. To me the damma is the more preferred of the two readings in this, although the other is also permissible and sound.

By His words ﴿And We have put a barrier before them and a barrier behind them﴾ He means that He adorned for them the evil of their deeds, so they wander blindly, and do not see the right guidance, and do not truly awaken.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe.﴾ (10) ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful in the unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.﴾ (11)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And it is the same for them, O Muhammad, whichever of the two you do toward them, warning or not warning, they will not believe, because God has already decreed that for them."

* *

As for His words ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Your warning, O Muhammad, benefits only the one who believes in the Qur'an and follows what it contains of God's commands, ﴿and fears the Most Merciful﴾," meaning: and fears God when he is out of sight of those who look on, not the hypocrite who makes light of God's religion when alone and shows faith before people, nor the polytheist upon whose heart God has set a seal.

* *

As for His words ﴿So give him good tidings of forgiveness﴾:

He says: "So give good tidings, O Muhammad, to this one who follows the Reminder and fears the Most Merciful in the unseen, of forgiveness from God for his sins, ﴿and a noble reward﴾," meaning: a generous reward from Him for him in the Hereafter, which is that He gives him Paradise for that deed.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿You can only warn one who follows the Reminder﴾: "Following the Reminder means following the Qur'an."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 12:

Interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life, and We record what they have sent forward and their traces, and We have enumerated everything in a clear record﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life﴾ from Our creation, ﴿and We record what they have sent forward﴾ in the world, of good and evil, and of righteous and wicked deeds.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life and We record what they have sent forward﴾: "From deeds."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his words ﴿and We record what they have sent forward﴾: "What they did."

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿what they have sent forward﴾: "Their deeds."

* * *

And His words ﴿and their traces﴾

That is: the traces of their steps with their feet. It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a people who wanted to move closer to the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that they would be nearer to it.

Those who said that:

* Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The dwellings of the Ansar were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move to the mosque, and then ﴿and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ was revealed, so they said: "We will remain in our place."

* Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Ansar's dwellings were far from the mosque, so they wanted to move. He said: Then ﴿and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ was revealed, so they remained.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: al-Juraiyri narrated to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir, who said: The Banu Salimah wanted to be close to the mosque. He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "O Banu Salimah, stay in your dwellings, for your traces are recorded."

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Kahmas narrate, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir, who said: The Banu Salimah wanted to relocate closer to the mosque, and the open land was empty. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "O Banu Salimah, stay in your dwellings, for your traces are recorded." He said: So they remained and said: "It does not please us that we had moved."

* Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Tarif, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Banu Salimah complained to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the distance of their dwellings, so ﴿Indeed, We bring the dead to life and We record what they have sent forward and their traces﴾ was revealed, and he said: "Remain in your dwellings; your traces are recorded."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Numaylah narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: I walked with Anas, and I quickened my pace, so he took my hand, and we walked slowly. When we had finished the prayer, Anas said: "I walked with Zayd ibn Thabit, and I quickened my pace, and he said: 'O Anas, do you not realise that traces are recorded?'"

* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, that the Banu Salimah's houses were remote from the mosque, so they intended to move close to the mosque to attend the prayer with the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Do you not seek reward for your traces, O Banu Salimah?" So they stayed in their dwellings.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding his words ﴿what they have sent forward and their traces﴾: "Their steps with their feet."

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and their traces﴾: "Their steps."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and their traces﴾: He said: al-Hasan said: "And their traces" means "their steps." Qatadah said: "If Allah had neglected anything of your affairs, O son of Adam, He would have neglected these traces that the winds efface."

* * *

And His words ﴿and We have enumerated everything in a clear record﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Everything that existed or will exist, We have enumerated, meaning We recorded it in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), which is the clear record (al-imam al-mubin). It has been said that it is called ﴿clear﴾ because it makes clear the reality of everything recorded in it.

The people of ta'wil have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in a clear record﴾: "In the Mother of the Book."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿and We have enumerated everything in a clear record﴾: "Everything enumerated with Allah is in a Book."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his words ﴿and We have enumerated everything in a clear record﴾: "The Mother of the Book, which is with Allah and in which all things are, is the clear record."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 13–14:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And set forth to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:13]. ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you."﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:14]

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And set forth to those of your people who associate partners with Allah, O Muhammad, a parable: the people of the town." It is mentioned that it was Antioch. ﴿When the messengers came to it﴾. The scholars differed concerning these messengers and concerning who had sent them to the people of the town. Some of them said: They were messengers of Jesus, son of Mary, and Jesus was the one who sent them to them.

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And set forth to them a parable: the people of the town, when the messengers came to it, when We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that Jesus, son of Mary, sent two men from the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) to Antioch, a city in the land of the Romans, and they denied them, so He strengthened them with a third. ﴿And they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you."﴾

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: al-Suddi narrated to me, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And set forth to them a parable: the people of the town﴾, he said: Antioch.

Others said: Rather, they were messengers whom Allah sent to them.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to us, as it reached him, from Ibn Abbas, and from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: In the city of Antioch there was a Pharaoh of the pharaohs called Abtayhas ibn Abtayhas, who worshipped idols, a man of polytheism. So Allah sent the messengers, and they were three: Sadiq, Masduq, and Salum. Two of them came to him and to the people of his city, and they denied them. Then Allah strengthened them with a third. When the messengers called him and proclaimed the command of Allah, and openly stated what they had been commanded, and criticized his religion and what they were upon, he said to them: ﴿Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you from us a painful punishment.﴾

And His saying: ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: when We sent to them two, calling them to Allah, and they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third and reinforced them with him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾, he said: We reinforced [them].

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾, he said: We added [to them].

- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾: We made them three. He said: That is the ta'azzuz (reinforcement), and ta'azzuz means strength.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you."﴾

He says: The three messengers said to the people of the town: Indeed, we are messengers to you, O people, to make worship purely for Allah alone, without partner, and to disavow what you worship of gods and idols.

Regarding His saying ﴿fa-'azzaznā﴾ (so We strengthened), the readers recited it with shaddah (doubling of the letter, 'azzaznā) other than 'Asim, who recited it without shaddah. The reading we hold to is with shaddah, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, and its meaning when doubled is "so We strengthened," and when unshaddah'd is "so We overpowered," and "overpowered" has little meaning in this context.

So Allah sent the messengers, and they were three: Sadiq, Masduq, and Salum. Two of them came to him and to the people of his city, and they denied them. Then Allah strengthened them with a third. When the messengers called him and proclaimed the command of Allah, and openly stated what they had been commanded, and criticized his religion and what they were upon, he said to them: ﴿Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you from us a painful punishment.﴾

And His saying: ﴿When We sent to them two, and they denied them, so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾.

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: when We sent to them two, calling them to Allah, and they denied them, so We strengthened them with a third and reinforced them with him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾, he said: We reinforced [them].

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾, he said: We added [to them].

- Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿so We strengthened [them] with a third﴾: We made them three. He said: That is the ta'azzuz (reinforcement), and ta'azzuz means strength.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they said, "Indeed, we are messengers to you."﴾

He says: The three messengers said to the people of the town: Indeed, we are messengers to you, O people, to make worship purely for Allah alone, without partner, and to disavow what you worship of gods and idols.

Regarding His saying ﴿fa-'azzaznā﴾ (so We strengthened), the readers recited it with shaddah (doubling of the letter, 'azzaznā) other than 'Asim, who recited it without shaddah. The reading we hold to is with shaddah, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it, and its meaning when doubled is "so We strengthened," and when unshaddah'd is "so We overpowered," and "overpowered" has little meaning in this context.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of the town said to the three men who were sent to them, when they informed them that they had been sent to them with what they had been sent with: "You, O people, are only men like us. Is it because you are admonished?﴾ They mean: your deeds and your provisions and your share of good and evil are with you. All of that is around your necks, and it is not from our ill omen if misfortune befalls you, but is what has been written for you and decreed for you by God.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Your omen is with you﴾: that is, your deeds are with you.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, as it reached him, from Ibn Abbas, and from Ka'b and from Wahb ibn Munabbih: the messengers said to them, ﴿Your omen is with you﴾, that is, your deeds are with you.

* *

As for His words ﴿Is it because you are admonished?﴾

The readings differ regarding this. The majority of the readers of the amsar (the major garrison cities) recited it ﴿أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾ with a kasra on the alif of "in" (إن) and a fatha on the interrogative alif (ألف الاستفهام), meaning: "If we admonish you, is your omen with you?" Then the interrogative alif was placed before "in", which is a conditional particle, according to the view of some grammarians of Basra, and according to the view of some Kufans it is understood as implying repetition, as if it were said: "Your omen is with you if you are admonished; your omen is with you," and the response was omitted, being indicated by the sense of the speech. The one who objected to the first view did so because the interrogative alif came between the condition and the conditional particle, so it cannot be a condition for what precedes the interrogative particle. It is related from Abu Razin that he recited it ﴿أَئِنْ ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾ meaning: "Is it because you were admonished that your omen is with you?" It is also reported that some of his readers recited it ﴿قَالُوا طَائِرُكُمْ مَعَكَمْ أَيْنَ ذُكِرْتُمْ﴾ meaning: "where you were admonished", with the kaf of "dhakartum" lightened.

The reading which we do not permit recitation other than by is the reading upon which the readers of the amsar agree, which is the entry of the interrogative alif upon the conditional particle, with the kaf of "dhukkirtum" doubled, in the sense we have mentioned from its readers, likewise, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Is it because you are admonished?﴾ that is: if we admonish you in God's name, do you take omen from us? ﴿Nay, but you are a people who exceed all bounds.﴾

* *

As for His words ﴿Nay, but you are a people who exceed all bounds﴾

He says: They said to them: "Your ill omen is not from us; rather you are a people who disobey God and commit sins, and sins and transgressions have overcome you."

* *

As for His words ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running﴾

He says: And there came from the farthest part of the city of these people to whom these messengers were sent a man running to them. That is because the people of this city resolved and their opinions united on killing these three messengers, as was mentioned. This reached this man, whose dwelling was at the farthest part of the city, and he was a believer, and his name, as was mentioned, was "Habib ibn Murri".

Reports have come in accordance with what we have said on this.

Mention of the reports related about this:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammil ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Mujallaz, who said: The companion of Ya Sin was "Habib ibn Murri".

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Among the account of the companion of Ya Sin is what:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, as it reached him, from Ibn Abbas, and from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, that he was a man from the people of Antioch, and his name was "Habib", and he used to work making rough wool cloth (al-jarir), and he was a sickly man, the leprosy having spread in him, and his dwelling was far off near one of the gates of the city, and he was a believer, possessing charity, gathering his earnings in the evening, as they mention, and dividing them into two halves: he feeds half to his dependents and gives half in charity. His sickness, his work and his weakness did not concern him from the work of his Lord. He said: When his people resolved to kill the messengers, this reached "Habib", who was at the farthest gate of the city, so he came running to them, reminding them of God and calling them to follow the messengers, and he said ﴿O my people, follow the messengers﴾.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'mar ibn Amr ibn Hazm, that it was related to him from Ka'b al-Ahbar, who said: Mention was made to him of Habib ibn Zayd ibn Asim, brother of the Banu Mazin ibn al-Najjar, whom Musaylimah the Liar cut into pieces at Yamamah when he began asking him about the Messenger of God ﷺ. He would say: "Do you testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of God?" and he would say: "Yes." Then he would say: "Do you testify that I am a messenger of God?" and he would say to him: "I do not hear." Musaylimah would say: "Do you hear this, and do not hear this?" and he would say: "Yes." So he kept cutting him limb by limb, and each time he asked him, he did not add to that, until he died in his hands. Ka'b said when it was said to him that his name was "Habib": "By God, he was the companion of Ya Sin, whose name was Habib."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Imarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Miqsam Abu al-Qasim, client of Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from Mujahid, from Abdullah ibn Abbas that he used to say: The name of the companion of Ya Sin was "Habib", and leprosy had spread in him.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running﴾: He said: It was mentioned to us that his name was "Habib", and he was in a cave worshipping his Lord, and when he heard of them he came to them.

* *

As for His words ﴿He said: "O my people, follow the messengers﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: The man who came from the farthest part of the city said to his people: "O my people, follow the messengers whom God has sent to you, and accept from them what they have brought you."

It is mentioned that when he came to the messengers, he asked them whether they sought any wage for what they had brought. The messengers said: "No." Then he said to his people at that point: "Follow those who ask you no wage for their counsel to you."

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: When he reached them, meaning the messengers, he said: "Do you ask any wage for this?" They said: "No." Then he said at that point ﴿O my people, follow the messengers. Follow those who ask you no wage, and who are rightly guided.﴾

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, as it reached him, from Ibn Abbas, and from Ka'b al-Ahbar, and from Wahb ibn Munabbih: ﴿Follow those who ask you no wage, and who are rightly guided﴾, that is: they do not ask you for your wealth in return for the guidance they have brought you, and they are sincere toward you, so follow them and you will be guided by their guidance.

* *

As for His words ﴿and who are rightly guided﴾

He says: They are upon the straight path of the truth, so be guided, O people, by their guidance.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 36, verses 26–27:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored."﴾

God, exalted is His remembrance, says: God said to him, when they had killed him in this manner and he met Him, ﴿"Enter Paradise."﴾ When he entered it and witnessed what God had honored him with because of his faith and his patience in it, ﴿he said, "Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me."﴾ That is, he says: "Would that they knew that the cause for which my Lord forgave my sins, and made me among those whom God honored by admitting me to His Paradise, was my faith in God and my patience in it, until I was killed, so that they might believe in God and deserve Paradise."

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from some of his companions, that Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to say: God said to him, "Enter Paradise," so he entered it alive, being provided for therein, and God had removed from him the sickness, sorrow and weariness of this world. When he reached the mercy of God, His Paradise and His honor, ﴿he said, "Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored."﴾

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words, ﴿"It was said, 'Enter Paradise.'"﴾ When he entered it, ﴿he said, "Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored."﴾ He said: "The believer meets no one except as an advisor, and he does not meet anyone as a deceiver. So when he witnessed the honor of God, ﴿he said, 'Would that my people knew of how my Lord has forgiven me and made me among the honored.'﴾ He wished upon God that his people might know what he witnessed of God's honor and what had overtaken him."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿"It was said, 'Enter Paradise.'"﴾ He said: "It was said: Paradise has become due to him." He said that when he saw the reward.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿"It was said, 'Enter Paradise.'"﴾ He said: "Paradise has become due to you."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, ﴿"It was said, 'Enter Paradise.'"﴾ He said: "Paradise has become due to him."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Mijlaz, regarding His words, ﴿"by which my Lord has forgiven me."﴾ He said: "My faith in my Lord and my affirmation of His messengers." And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 28–29:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down,﴾ ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾

Exalted is He, says: And We did not send down upon the people of this believer, whom his people killed for calling them to God and advising them, ﴿after him﴾, meaning: after his destruction, ﴿any host from the heaven﴾.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of the "host" that God informed was not sent down upon the people of this believer after they killed him. Some of them said: What is meant is that God did not send down to them after that any message (risalah), nor did He send them a prophet.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿any host from the heaven﴾: "A message."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down,﴾ he said: "By God, God did not rebuke his people after killing him, ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾"

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that God, mentioned be His remembrance, did not raise up for them armies to fight them with, but He destroyed them with one shout.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from some of his companions, that 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: God became angry on his behalf, meaning on behalf of this believer, because of their oppressing him, with an anger that left nothing of the people; so He hastened retribution upon them for what they had made lawful from him. And He said: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down,﴾ meaning: We did not outnumber them with multitudes; the matter was easier for Us than that. ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾ So God destroyed that king and the people of Antioch, and they perished from the face of the earth, and not one survivor remained among them.

This second opinion is the more preferred of the two interpretations of the verse, because a message (risalah) is not called a "host" (jund), unless Mujahid meant by it the messengers, in which case it would be a possible reading; yet it is also, by the apparent sense of the verse, far-fetched, since messengers from among the sons of Adam do not descend from the heaven, and the report in the apparent wording of this verse, that He did not send down from the heaven after the destruction of this believer upon his people any host, is more fitting for angels than for the sons of Adam.

* *

And His saying: ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾

Meaning: Their destruction was only one shout that God sent down upon them from the heaven.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the metropolitan cities recited ﴿إِنْ كَانَتْ إِلا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ with a fatha (naṣb) on the interpretation I have mentioned, with an implied subject in kānat (the pronoun of the subject being understood). It is related from Abu Ja'far al-Madani that he recited it ﴿إلا صيْحَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾ with a damma (raf'), on the basis that it is the subject of kāna, and there is no implied pronoun in kāna.

The correct recitation in this matter, in my view, is the naṣb, due to the consensus of the authorities (ijma' al-hujjah) upon it, and upon there being an implied pronoun in kānat.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Then immediately they were extinguished.﴾

Meaning: Then immediately they were dead, perished.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 28–29:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down,﴾ ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾

Exalted is He, says: And We did not send down upon the people of this believer, whom his people killed for calling them to God and advising them, ﴿after him﴾, meaning: after his destruction, ﴿any host from the heaven﴾.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of the "host" that God informed was not sent down upon the people of this believer after they killed him. Some of them said: What is meant is that God did not send down to them after that any message (risalah), nor did He send them a prophet.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying ﴿any host from the heaven﴾: "A message."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down,﴾ he said: "By God, God did not rebuke his people after killing him, ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾"

Others said: Rather, what is meant is that God, mentioned be His remembrance, did not raise up for them armies to fight them with, but He destroyed them with one shout.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, from some of his companions, that 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: God became angry on his behalf, meaning on behalf of this believer, because of their oppressing him, with an anger that left nothing of the people; so He hastened retribution upon them for what they had made lawful from him. And He said: ﴿And We did not send down upon his people after him any host from the heaven, nor were We ever going to send down,﴾ meaning: We did not outnumber them with multitudes; the matter was easier for Us than that. ﴿It was but one shout, and immediately they were extinguished.﴾ So God destroyed that king and the people of Antioch, and they perished from the face of the earth, and not one survivor remained among them.

This second opinion is the more preferred of the two interpretations of the verse, because a message (risalah) is not called a "host" (jund), unless Mujahid meant by it the messengers, in which case it would be a possible reading; yet it is also, by the apparent sense of the verse, far-fetched, since messengers from among the sons of Adam do not descend from the heaven, and the report in the apparent wording of this verse, that He did not send down from the heaven after the destruction of this believer upon his people any host, is more fitting for angels than for the sons of Adam.

Meaning: Their destruction was only one shout that God sent down upon them from the heaven.

**The interpretation of His word, exalted is He: ﴿Alas for the servants! No messenger comes to them but they mock him﴾ (36:30)**

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: "Alas, O regret from the servants over themselves, and remorse and anguish, for their mocking of the messengers of God ﴿no messenger comes to them﴾ from God ﴿but they mock him﴾." He mentioned that this is in some readings: ﴿Alas for the regret of the servants over themselves﴾ (*yā ḥasrata al-ʿibād ʿalā anfusihā*).

Those who interpret (*ahl al-taʾwīl*, the exegetes) have said something similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Alas, O regret, from the servants﴾, meaning: O regret of the servants over themselves, over what they neglected of the command of God and what they fell short of in the right of God. He said: In some readings it is: ﴿Alas for the regret of the servants over themselves﴾.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding his saying ﴿Alas, O regret, from the servants﴾: He said: It was a regret upon them, their mocking of the messengers.

⁕ ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding his saying ﴿Alas, O regret, from the servants﴾: He says: Woe, O servants.

And some of the grammarians (*ahl al-ʿarabiyyah*) used to say: The meaning of that is: "How great is the regret over the servants!"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 31–32:

The explanation of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?(31) And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us, present.(32)﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these polytheists among your people not seen, O Muhammad, how many We destroyed before them, because of their denial of Our messengers and their disbelief in Our signs, from the generations of the past ﴿that they do not return to them﴾? That is, have they not seen that they do not return to them?

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them, that they do not return to them?﴾ He said: 'Ad and Thamud, and many generations between them.

And "kam" in His saying ﴿how many We destroyed﴾ is in the accusative position, if you wish, by the governing of "yarawa" (they have seen) upon it. It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) it is: ﴿Have they not seen whom We destroyed﴾. And if you wish, it is governed by "ahlakna" (We destroyed) upon it. As for "annahum", its alif is fathah by the governing of "yarawa" upon it. It is mentioned from some of them that he read the alif of it with kasrah, as a fresh start (isti'naf), leaving "yarawa" without governing it.

And His saying ﴿And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us, present﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And indeed, all these generations that We destroyed, and those whom We did not destroy and others, will be present with Us on the Day of Resurrection, all of them brought forth.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And indeed, all of them will be brought before Us, present﴾: that is, they on the Day of Resurrection.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basrah, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿wa-in kullun lamma﴾ with the lightened (mim), directing it to the understanding that "ma" was added to it, with the lam that enters as the answer to "in" (indeed), and the meaning of the speech being: and indeed all of them are, certainly, present before Us. The majority of the reciters of Kufah recited ﴿lammā﴾ with the mim doubled (shaddah). For their doubling there are, in our view, two explanations. The first: that the speech in their view was intended as: wa-in kullun lamma jamī', then one of the two mims was dropped because they were many, as the poet said:

"At the morning when the scholars of Bakr ibn Wa'il floated [in the water], and we turned the chests of the horses toward Tamim..." [[This is a verse from a poem which al-Baladhuri in "Ansab al-Ashraf" attributes to Salih ibn Abd Allah al-Abshami the Kharijite, in fighting Harithah ibn Badr al-Ghudani against the Azariqah, before al-Muhallab fought them. Al-Mubarrad in al-Kamil attributes it to Qatari ibn al-Fujaa'ah the Kharijite, on the day of Dulab. The narration of al-Baladhuri is "tafat fi al-ma'" and that of al-Mubarrad is "tafat 'ulama'". Its original is "'ala al-ma'", as you say of the Banu al-Harith: "bi-al-Harith". The verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 269), where he said: As for His saying (wa-in kullun lamma jami'), al-A'mash and Asim doubled it (lamma), while a large number of the reciters of Madinah lightened it. It has reached me that Ali lightened it, and that is the correct form, because "ma" was added to it with a lam which serves as the answer to "in", as if you said: wa-in kullun lamma jami' ladayna muhdarun; and none transmitted its heavier form except from correctness. If you wish, you intend: wa-in kullun "lamman ma" jami', then one of the mims was dropped because of their multiplicity, as the poet said "at the morning when the scholars floated..." the verse. The other way of the heavy reading: that they make "lamma" equivalent to "illa" (except), as if "lam" had "ma" joined to it, so they became one word, and left the sphere of negation. Al-Kisa'i used to deny this view, saying: I do not know the aspect of "lamma" in the doubled reading in recitation.] Abu Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 204): "wa-in kull": when you lighten "in" you raise with it, and if you make it heavy you put it in the accusative. "Lamma jami'" its explanation: wa-in kullun la-jami'. And "ma" its metaphorical function is like (mathalan ma ba'udah) and (amma qalil).

The other: that they intended "lamma" to mean "illa" (except) only with "in", so it becomes the parallel of "innama" when placed in the position of "illa". Some grammarians of Kufah used to say: it is as if "lam" had "ma" joined to it, so both became an exception, and they left the sphere of negation. Some Arabic scholars used to say: I do not know the aspect of "lamma" with doubling.

The correct statement on this, in my view, is that they are two well-known readings, close in meaning; so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 33–34:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And a sign for them is the dead earth; We have revived it and brought forth from it grain, and from it they eat. And We placed therein gardens of date palms and grapevines, and We caused springs to gush forth within it﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And a proof for these polytheists of God's power over what He wills, and over His reviving those of His creatures who have died and restoring them after their annihilation, just as He was before their death, is His reviving the dead earth, which has no plant or crop in it, by the rain that He sends down from the sky until its crop comes forth, and then His bringing forth from it the grain, which is their sustenance and nourishment, so from it they eat.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We placed therein gardens of date palms and grapevines﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And We placed in this earth, which We revived after its death, orchards of date palms and grapevines. ﴿And We caused springs to gush forth within it from the water-sources﴾ meaning: and We caused to spring forth in it springs of water.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 35–36:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That they may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands have made. Will they not then give thanks?﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, means: We created these gardens in this land so that My servants may eat of its fruit, and of what their hands have made. He means: that they may eat of the fruit of the gardens which We created for them, and of what their hands have made, namely what they planted and sowed themselves. The "ma" in His saying ﴿and of what their hands have made﴾ is in the genitive position, coordinated with "al-thamar" (the fruit), meaning: and of that which their hands have made. In the reading attributed to Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), it is ﴿wa-mimma 'amilathu﴾ with the pronoun (ha') expressed, in accordance with this meaning. The pronoun in our reading is therefore implied, since the Arabs sometimes omit it and sometimes express it in relative clauses after "min", "ma" and "alladhi". If "ma" were said to be a verbal noun (masdar), it would also be a valid view, so the meaning of the sentence would be: and of the work of their hands. And if it were said that it is a negation (al-jahd) with no grammatical position, that too would be a valid view, so the meaning of the sentence would be: that they may eat of its fruit, and their hands did not make it.

* *

And His saying ﴿Will they not then give thanks?﴾

He says: Will these people not give thanks to the One who provided them with this sustenance from this dead land, which We brought to life for them, the One who provided them with that and bestowed favour upon them with it?

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to Him who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows, and of themselves, and of what they do not know.﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, glorifying and declaring free of imperfection the One who created all the different kinds, of the plants of the earth, and of themselves. He means: and He created, from their offspring, males and females, and of what they also do not know, of things which He has not made known to them, He likewise created pairs, of what these polytheists ascribe to Him, of partners and other things they attribute to Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 37–38:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs on to a station for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And a proof for them too, of God's power to do all that He wills: ﴿the night, from which We strip the day﴾, meaning: We pull the day off it. The meaning of "minhu" (from it) in this place is "'anhu" (from it/away from it), as if it were said: We strip the day away from it, so We bring darkness and take away the daylight. Among its like is His saying: ﴿And recite to them the tidings of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he stripped himself from them﴾, meaning: he departed from them and left them. Likewise the stripping of the night from the day.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿behold, they are in darkness﴾

It means: then they have become in darkness by the coming of the night.

Qatadah said concerning this, as related to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness﴾: He said: He causes the night to enter into the day, and causes the day to enter into the night. But what Qatadah said on this, in my view, regarding the meaning of stripping the day from the night, is far-fetched. That is because the entering of the night into the day is only the addition of what has been lost of the hours of one to the hours of the other, and stripping has nothing to do with that, since the day is stripped from the whole night, and likewise the night from the whole day, whereas it is not the case that all the night enters into all the day, nor all the day into all the night.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a station for it﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And the sun runs to the place of its resting, meaning: towards its place of rest; and it has come in a report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to this effect.

Mention of the narration to this effect:

Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dhar al-Ghifari, who said: I was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) in the mosque when the sun set. He said: "O Abu Dhar, do you know where the sun goes?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes and prostrates before its Lord, then it asks permission to return, and permission is granted to it. It is as if it is said to it: 'Return from where you came,' so it rises from its place, and that is its station."

Others among them said concerning this, as related to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And the sun runs on to a station for it﴾: He said: a single fixed time which it does not exceed.

Others said: the meaning of this is: it runs to a course for it, to the measures of its places, meaning: it runs to its furthest setting-point, then it returns and does not go beyond it. They said: That is because it keeps advancing every night until it reaches its furthest setting-points, and then it returns.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾

He says: This which We have described, of the sun's running to a station for it, is the decree of the Almighty in His vengeance against His enemies, the All-Knowing of the interests of His creatures and of all other things; nothing hidden is concealed from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 37–38:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness. And the sun runs on to a station for it. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And a proof for them too, of God's power to do all that He wills: ﴿the night, from which We strip the day﴾, meaning: We pull the day off it. The meaning of "minhu" (from it) in this place is "'anhu" (from it/away from it), as if it were said: We strip the day away from it, so We bring darkness and take away the daylight. Among its like is His saying: ﴿And recite to them the tidings of him to whom We gave Our signs, but he stripped himself from them﴾, meaning: he departed from them and left them. Likewise the stripping of the night from the day.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿behold, they are in darkness﴾

It means: then they have become in darkness by the coming of the night.

Qatadah said concerning this, as related to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness﴾: He said: He causes the night to enter into the day, and causes the day to enter into the night. But what Qatadah said on this, in my view, regarding the meaning of stripping the day from the night, is far-fetched. That is because the entering of the night into the day is only the addition of what has been lost of the hours of one to the hours of the other, and stripping has nothing to do with that, since the day is stripped from the whole night, and likewise the night from the whole day, whereas it is not the case that all the night enters into all the day, nor all the day into all the night.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the sun runs on to a station for it﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And the sun runs to the place of its resting, meaning: towards its place of rest; and it has come in a report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to this effect.

Mention of the narration to this effect:

Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from Abu Dhar al-Ghifari, who said: I was sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) in the mosque when the sun set. He said: "O Abu Dhar, do you know where the sun goes?" I said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "It goes and prostrates before its Lord, then it asks permission to return, and permission is granted to it. It is as if it is said to it: 'Return from where you came,' so it rises from its place, and that is its station."

Others among them said concerning this, as related to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And the sun runs on to a station for it﴾: He said: a single fixed time which it does not exceed.

Others said: the meaning of this is: it runs to a course for it, to the measures of its places, meaning: it runs to its furthest setting-point, then it returns and does not go beyond it. They said: That is because it keeps advancing every night until it reaches its furthest setting-points, and then it returns.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾

He says: This which We have described, of the sun's running to a station for it, is the decree of the Almighty in His vengeance against His enemies, the All-Knowing of the interests of His creatures and of all other things; nothing hidden is concealed from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 39–40:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And the moon — We have measured for it stations until it returns like the old dry date-stalk (ʿurjūn). (39) It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each is traveling in an orbit (falak), swimming along.﴾ (40)

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿And the moon, We have measured it in stations﴾. Some Meccan readers, some Medinan readers and some Basran readers read ﴿wal-qamaru﴾ (and the moon) in the nominative, conjoining it to the sun, since the sun was conjoined to the night; they likewise made the moon follow the sun in its i'rab (grammatical case), because it too is among the signs, just as the night and the day are two signs. According to this reading, the sense of the statement is: "And a sign for them is the moon: We have measured it in stations." Other Meccan readers, other Medinan readers, other Basran readers, and the majority of the readers of Kufa read it in the accusative, ﴿wal-qamara qaddarnāhu﴾ (and the moon, We have measured it), meaning: "and We have measured the moon in stations, as We did with the sun," thus returning it, in meaning, to the pronoun in "the sun," because the waw in it introduces a following verb.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known recitations and both are sound in meaning; whichever of them a reader recites is correct. The sense of the statement is: "And a sign for them is that Our measuring of the moon into stations results in its waning after its fullness, its completeness and its evenness, until it returns like the old ʿurjūn." The ʿurjūn (the stalk of the bunch of dates, from the place where it grows on the palm to the place of the shamārīkh, the small strands of the cluster). Glory be to Him, He likened it to the old ʿurjūn; the "old" (qadīm) is the dry one, because that (the stalk of the cluster) is found only bent and curved when it ages and dries, and is hardly ever found straight and upright like the branches and boughs of other trees. Likewise the moon, when it is at the end of the month before it becomes hidden, takes on, in its curvature and bending, the likeness of that ʿurjūn.

Those who expounded the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿until it returns like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: the origin of the ʿidhq is the old one.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿until it returns like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he meant by the ʿurjūn: the dry ʿidhq.

- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿And the moon, We have measured it in stations until it returns like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: like the ʿidhq of the palm when it becomes old and bends.

- Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to me, saying: Abu Yazid al-Kharraz related to us, meaning Khalid ibn Hayyan al-Raqqi, from Jaʿfar ibn Burqan, from Yazid ibn al-Asamm, regarding His saying ﴿until it returns like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: the ʿidhq of the palm when it becomes old and bends.

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: ʿIsa ibn ʿUbayd related to us, from ʿIkrima, regarding His saying ﴿like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: the old palm.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Israʾil informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, ﴿like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: the dry ʿidhq.

- Muhammad ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAli al-Muqaddami and Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, both saying: Abu ʿAsim and al-Muqaddami related to us, saying: I heard Abu ʿAsim say: I heard Sulayman al-Taymi, regarding His saying ﴿until it returns like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: the ʿidhq.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, ﴿until it returns like the old ʿurjūn﴾: he said: God measured it into stations, so it kept waning until it was like the ʿidhq of the palm; He likened it to the ʿidhq of the palm.

* *

As for His saying ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾

He, may He be exalted, says: It is not fitting for the sun that it should reach the moon, so that its light would be extinguished by its light and all the times would be day with no night in them. ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: He, may He be exalted, says: nor does the night pass ahead of the day so that its darkness vanishes by its brightness, and all the times would be night.

Those who expounded the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said, though they differed in their wording in interpreting this; yet the meaning of most of them is what we have stated.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from ʿAnbasa, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾: he said: its light does not resemble the light of the other; it is not fitting for it.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾: he said: the light of neither resembles the light of the other, nor is that fitting for them.

Regarding His saying ﴿nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: he said: they pursue each other rapidly, one stripping off from the other.

- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: al-Ashja'i related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: he said: the light of this does not overtake the light of that, nor does that overtake the light of this.

- I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon﴾: this concerns the light of the moon and the light of the sun; when the sun rises there is no light for the moon, and when the moon rises with its light there is no light for the sun. ﴿Nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: he said: in God's decree and knowledge, the night does not outstrip the day so as to reach it and vanish its darkness, and in God's decree the day does not outstrip the night so as to reach it and vanish its light.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: each has a limit and a knowledge it does not exceed, nor does it fall short of it; when the authority of this one comes, the authority of that one departs, and when the authority of that one comes, the authority of this one departs.

It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding this:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon nor does the night outstrip the day﴾: he said: when the two are together in the sky, one of them is before the other; when they set, one of them sets before the other. And "an" (that) in His saying ﴿an tudrika﴾ is in a position of nominative case following the verb "yanbaghi" (it is fitting).

* *

As for His saying ﴿And each is in an orbit, swimming﴾

He says: all that we have mentioned, the sun, the moon, the night and the day, travel in an orbit.

Those who expounded the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Hakam ibn ʿAbd Allah al-ʿIjli related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from Muslim al-Batin, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas (And each is in an orbit, swimming): he said: in an orbit like the orbit of the spindle (mighzal).

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, saying: al-Aʿmash related to us, from Muslim al-Batin, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, the like of it.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: the course of each of them, meaning the night and the day, "in an orbit they swim": they run.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, ﴿And each is in an orbit, swimming﴾: i.e., in the orbit of the heaven they swim.

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And each is in an orbit, swimming﴾: "revolving"; he says: revolving they swim; he says: they run.

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And each is in an orbit, swimming﴾: he means: each in an orbit in the heavens?
