Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 36, verses 41–44:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾ [36:41]

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And a proof for them as well, and a sign of Our power over whatever We will: We carried their offspring, meaning whoever was saved of the descendants of Adam in the ship of Noah. It is this that He, may His praise be exalted, meant by "the laden ship." Al-fulk (the ship) is the vessel, and al-mashhun (laden) means filled, heavily loaded.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾: he said: "al-mamtali" (the full).

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿in the laden ship﴾: he meant "al-muthaqal" (the heavily weighted).

- Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sallt related to us, saying: Abu Kudaynah related to us, from Ata', from Sa'id, ﴿al-fulk al-mashhun﴾, he said: "al-mawqar" (the heavily loaded).

- Imran ibn Musa related to us, saying: Abd al-Warith related to us, saying: Yunus related to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿al-mashhun﴾, he said: "al-mahmul" (the carried).

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾: he meant the ship of Noah, peace be upon him.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship﴾: "al-mawqar," meaning the ship of Noah.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿al-fulk al-mashhun﴾: "The laden ship is the vessel in which Noah was, and the offspring who were in that vessel." He said: "al-mashhun" is that which has been loaded, which has been prepared for its people to ride, into which they put whatever they wished, so it may be full and it may not be full.

- Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Do you know what the laden ship is?" We said: "No." He said: "It is the heavily loaded one (al-mawqar)."

- Amr ibn Abd al-Hamid al-Amili related to us, saying: Harun related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿al-fulk al-mashhun﴾: "al-mawqar."

- Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Do you know what ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾ is?" We said: "No." He said: "They are ships, made after the ship of Noah, in its likeness."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "Small ships."

- He said: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "Small ships. Do you not see that He said ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no helper for them﴾?"

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur ibn Zadhan, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "Small ships."

- Hatim ibn Bakr al-Dabbi related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Umar related to us, from Shu'bah, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih: ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "Small ships."

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: he meant the ships that were made after it, meaning after the ship of Noah.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "They are the ships from which benefit is derived."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "And these are the vessels."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubayd related to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "Yes, of the like of a ship."

Others said: rather, it means camels.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to us, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "He means camels. God created them as you have seen; they are the ships of the land, on which they are carried and which they ride."

- Nasr ibn Ali related to us, saying: Ghundar related to us, from Uthman ibn Ghiyath, from Ikrimah, regarding ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "Camels."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Abdullah ibn Shaddad said regarding ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "They are camels."

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And We created for them of the like thereof that which they ride﴾: "From the cattle (al-an'am)."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said: "They are camels."

The view most fitting for the interpretation of this is the saying of the one who said that it means ships, because of the indication of His saying ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no helper for them﴾ that this is so; for drowning is known to occur only in water, and there is no drowning on land.

* *

And His saying ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no helper for them﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And if We will, We drown these polytheists when they ride the ship on the sea, ﴿and there is no helper for them﴾, meaning: there is no one to rescue them when We drown them, who would save them from drowning.

As related:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And if We will, We drown them, and there is no helper for them﴾: i.e., there is no rescuer (mughith).

* *

And His saying ﴿nor are they rescued﴾

He says: Nor does anything rescue them from drowning if We drown them in the sea, except that We rescue them out of Our mercy toward them, and deliver them from it.

* *

And His saying ﴿but as a mercy from Us, and an enjoyment for a time﴾

He says: And We let them enjoy (their lives) until a term they will reach. It is as if He said: nor are they rescued, except that We show them mercy and let them enjoy (life) until a term.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and an enjoyment for a time﴾: i.e., until death.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 45–46:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you, that perhaps you may receive mercy,"﴾ and ﴿Never does there come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When it is said to these polytheists, who associate others with Allah and deny His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), "Beware of what has passed before you of the punishments and retributions of Allah, [and] of what befell those who were struck by it among the nations before you, lest the like of it befall you for your polytheism and your denial of His Messenger." ﴿And what is behind you﴾ means: what lies after your destruction, which you will meet if you perish in the disbelief in which you are. ﴿That perhaps you may receive mercy﴾ means: that your Lord may have mercy upon you if you take heed of that and fear Him by repenting of your polytheism, believing in Him, and adhering to His obedience in what He has made obligatory upon you of His duties.

And in accordance with what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you"﴾: "the events of Allah concerning those who passed before them among the nations, and what is behind them of the matter of the Hour."

Mujahid used to say concerning this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿what is before you﴾: "what has passed of their sins." This statement is close in meaning to the statement we have given, because its meaning is: "Beware the punishment for what is before you of your sins, and what is behind you of the sins you commit which you have not yet committed." So this is a warning to them of punishment for their disbelief.

* *

And His saying ﴿And never does there come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: No sign comes to these polytheists of Quraysh, meaning a proof from the proofs of Allah and an indication of His signs regarding the truth of His oneness and the confirmation of His Messenger, except that they turn away from it, not reflecting upon it nor contemplating it, so that they would know by it what Allah has argued against them through it.

If someone says: Where is the response to His saying ﴿And when it is said to them, "Beware of what is before you and what is behind you"﴾? It is said: its response and the response to His saying ﴿Never does there come to them a sign from the signs of their Lord﴾ ...

* *

His saying ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾

Because their turning away was from every sign of Allah, the answer was sufficed, regarding His saying ﴿Beware of what is before you﴾ and regarding His saying ﴿Never does there come to them a sign﴾, by the report of their turning away from them. That is because the meaning of the speech is: "And when it is said to them, 'Beware of what is before you and what is behind you,' they turn away; and when a sign comes to them, they turn away."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 47–48:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend from what Allah has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed? You are not but in clear error."﴾ (36:47)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And when it is said to these polytheists who associate others with Allah, "Spend from the provision of Allah that He has given you, and discharge from it what Allah has obligated you to give to the needy and the poor," the ones who denied the oneness of Allah and worshipped others besides Him say to the believers in Allah and His Messenger, "Shall we feed with our wealth and our food one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed?"

As for His saying, ﴿You are not but in clear error﴾, there are two possible readings. The first is that it is part of the speech of the disbelievers to the believers, so the meaning of the statement then is: "You, O people, in your saying to us, 'Spend from what Allah has provided you upon your needy,' are not but in a departure from the truth and a deviation from right guidance, clear to whoever considers and reflects that you are in error." This is the preferable of the two readings in its interpretation. The second reading is that this is part of the speech of Allah to the polytheists, so its interpretation then is: "You, O disbelievers, in your saying to the believers, 'Shall we feed one whom, if Allah willed, He would feed,' are not but in clear error, in that your saying that to them is error."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"﴾ (36:48)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And these polytheists who deny the threat of Allah and the resurrection after death say, seeking to hasten their Lord's punishment, ﴿When is this promise?﴾ That is, the promise of the establishment of the Hour, ﴿if you should be truthful﴾, O people. This is their saying to the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 49–50:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They await but a single Cry, which will seize them while they are disputing [yakhissimun]﴾ ﴿So they will not be able to make a bequest, nor return to their families﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: What are these polytheists waiting for, those who hasten the threat of God against them, except a single Cry that will seize them? That is the blast of terror (nafkhat al-faza') at the establishment of the Hour.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this, and reports have come down.

Mention of those who said that and what is in it of report: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiyy and Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, both saying: 'Awf ibn Abi Jamilah related to us, from Abu al-Mughira al-Qawwas, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: "The Trumpet will indeed be blown while people are on their paths, their markets and their gatherings, so that a garment will be between two men haggling over it, and neither of them will let it go from his hand until the Trumpet is blown. And a man will set out from his house and will not return until the Trumpet is blown." And this is the one of which God said: ﴿They await but a single Cry, which will seize them while they are disputing. So they will not be able to make a bequest﴾ ... the verse.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿They await but a single Cry, which will seize them while they are disputing﴾: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "The Hour will come upon the people while a man is watering his livestock, and a man is repairing his pool, and a man is displaying his goods in his market, and a man is lowering and raising his scale, and it will come upon them while they are in that state, so they will not be able to make a bequest, nor return to their families."

⁕ Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿They await but a single Cry﴾: the blast is one blast.

⁕ Abu Kuraib related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi related to us, from Isma'il ibn Rafi', from one whom he mentioned, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet and gave it to Israfil. He places it at his mouth, gazing with his eye toward the Throne, awaiting when he will be commanded. Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of God, what is the Trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: And what is it like? He said: A great horn into which three blasts will be blown. The first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of swooning, and the third is the blast of standing before the Lord of the worlds. God commands Israfil with the first blast, and he says: Blow the blast of terror. So the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. God commands him and he prolongs it and extends it, and it does not cease. This is the one of which God says: ﴿And these await but a single Cry, for which there is no respite [fawaq]﴾. Then God commands Israfil with the blast of swooning, and he says: Blow the blast of swooning. So the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth will swoon, except whom God wills. Then they will be lifeless. Then He causes to die whoever remains, until none remains except God, the One, the Eternal Refuge. He will change the earth to other than the earth and the heavens, and He will spread it out and flatten it, and stretch it like a tanned hide of 'Ukaz; you will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness. Then God will drive the creatures with one driving, and they will be in this changed earth in the same places they were in the first, whatever was in its belly will be in its belly, and whatever was on its back will be on its back."

The reciters differed in the reading of His saying ﴿wa-hum yakhissimun﴾. Some reciters of Medina read ﴿wa-hum yakhsimmun﴾ with the kha' quiescent and the sad doubled, combining two quiescent letters, meaning yakhtasimun; then they assimilated the ta' into the sad, making it a doubled sad, and left the kha' quiescent as it originally is. Some Meccan and Basran reciters read ﴿wa-hum yakhassimun﴾ with the kha' fathah and the sad doubled, meaning yakhtasimun, except that they transferred the vowel of the ta' — which is the fathah in yafta'ilun — to the kha' before it, moving it by its movement, and assimilated the ta' into the sad and doubled it. Some reciters of Kufa read ﴿yakhissimun﴾ with the kha' kasrah and the sad doubled, making the kha' kasrah by the kasrah of the sad, and assimilated the ta' into the sad and doubled it. Others read ﴿yakhsimun﴾ with the kha' quiescent and the sad light, meaning ﴿yaf'ilun﴾ from khusumah (disputation), and the sense for the one who reads thus is as if they were speaking, or its meaning for him is: they were, in their own estimation, disputing with the one who promised them the coming of the Hour and the establishment of the Resurrection, and overcoming him with argument concerning it.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that these are well-known readings, recognized among the reciters of the regions, close in meaning; so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct.

* *

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: So these polytheists, at the blowing of the Trumpet, will not be able to bequeath their wealth to anyone ﴿nor return to their families﴾. That is: nor will whoever among them is away from his family be able to return to them, because they will not be given respite for that, but will be hastened to destruction.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 54–55:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in the least, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾ [36:54], ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾ [36:55].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿So today﴾ meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿no soul will be wronged in the least﴾. Likewise, our Lord does not wrong any soul in the least: He does not withhold from it the reward of its righteous deeds, nor does He lay upon it the burden of another's sin. Rather, He pays every soul the reward of the good it has done, and He punishes it only for what it has committed and acquired. ﴿And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾ means: you will not be repaid except with the recompense of your deeds which you used to do in the world.

* *

And His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of the "occupation" (shughl) with which Allah, may His praise be exalted, described the companions of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: it is the deflowering of virgins.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: their occupation is the deflowering of virgins.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from Abu 'Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: the deflowering of virgins.

- Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: the deflowering of virgins.

- al-Hasan ibn Zurayq al-Tuhawi related to me, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Suda'i related to me, saying: Abu al-Nadr related to us, from al-Ashja'i, from Wa'il ibn Dawud, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: in the deflowering of virgins.

And others said: rather, what is meant by it is that they are in bounty.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy﴾, he said: in bounty.

- 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: Marwan related to us, from Juwaybir, from Abu Sahl, from al-Hasan, regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise﴾ ... the verse, he said: their occupation is the bounty, which preoccupies them from what the people of the Fire are in of punishment.

And others said: rather, the meaning of that is that they are occupied away from what the people of the Fire are in.

Those who said this:

- Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Shu'bah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise﴾ ... the verse, he said: they are in an occupation away from what the people of the Fire encounter.

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is to say as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise﴾, who are its people, ﴿are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, with bounties that come to them while they are occupied. That occupation in which they are is a bounty, and the deflowering of virgins, and diversion and pleasure, and being occupied away from what the people of the Fire encounter.

The readers differed concerning the reading of His saying ﴿fi shughul﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Basrans, with variation from them, read ﴿fi shughlin﴾ with a damma on the shin and a sukun on the ghayn. It is related from Abu 'Amr that he read it with a damma on the shin and a sukun on the ghayn, and with a fatha on both the shin and the ghayn, as shaghl. Some of the people of Medina and Basra and the majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿fi shughulin﴾ with a damma on both the shin and the ghayn.

In my view, the correct reading is with a damma on both the shin and the ghayn, or with a damma on the shin and a sukun on the ghayn; whichever of these the reader recites is correct, because that is the well-known reading among the readers of the regions, with the two meanings being close. As for reading it with a fatha on both the shin and the ghayn, it is not permissible in my view, because the consensus of the authoritative readers is against it.

They also differed concerning the reading of His saying ﴿fakihun﴾. The majority of the readers of the regions read ﴿fakihun﴾ with an alif. It is mentioned from Abu Ja'far al-Qari that he read it ﴿fakihun﴾ without an alif.

In my view, the correct reading is the one who read it with the alif, because that is the well-known reading.

The interpreters differed concerning its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is ﴿farihun﴾, joyful.

Those who said this:

- 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿fi shughlin fakihun﴾, he says: joyful.

And others said: its meaning is ﴿'ajibun﴾, amazed.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿fakihun﴾, he said: amazed.

- al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿fakihun﴾, he said: amazed.

The Arabs say of a man who enjoys food or fruit, or the honour of people: "Indeed so-and-so is fakih with the honour of people." Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 54–55:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿So today no soul will be wronged in the least, and you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾ [36:54], ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾ [36:55].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿So today﴾ meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿no soul will be wronged in the least﴾. Likewise, our Lord does not wrong any soul in the least: He does not withhold from it the reward of its righteous deeds, nor does He lay upon it the burden of another's sin. Rather, He pays every soul the reward of the good it has done, and He punishes it only for what it has committed and acquired. ﴿And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do﴾ means: you will not be repaid except with the recompense of your deeds which you used to do in the world.

* *

And His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾.

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of the "occupation" (shughl) with which Allah, may His praise be exalted, described the companions of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: it is the deflowering of virgins.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: their occupation is the deflowering of virgins.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, from Abu 'Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: the deflowering of virgins.

- Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: the deflowering of virgins.

- al-Hasan ibn Zurayq al-Tuhawi related to me, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad related to us, from his father, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

- al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Suda'i related to me, saying: Abu al-Nadr related to us, from al-Ashja'i, from Wa'il ibn Dawud, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, he said: in the deflowering of virgins.

And others said: rather, what is meant by it is that they are in bounty.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise today are busy﴾, he said: in bounty.

- 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: Marwan related to us, from Juwaybir, from Abu Sahl, from al-Hasan, regarding the saying of Allah, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise﴾ ... the verse, he said: their occupation is the bounty, which preoccupies them from what the people of the Fire are in of punishment.

And others said: rather, the meaning of that is that they are occupied away from what the people of the Fire are in.

Those who said this:

- Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Shu'bah, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise﴾ ... the verse, he said: they are in an occupation away from what the people of the Fire encounter.

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is to say as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, the companions of Paradise﴾, who are its people, ﴿are busy in a joyful occupation﴾, with bounties that come to them while they are occupied. That occupation in which they are is a bounty, and the deflowering of virgins, and diversion and pleasure, and being occupied away from what the people of the Fire encounter.

By His saying ﴿They﴾, He, may He be exalted, means the people of Paradise, ﴿and their spouses﴾ among the people of Paradise, in Paradise.

As [was transmitted]:

⁕ Al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waqqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿They and their spouses are in shade﴾, he said: "their wives, in shades (zilal)."

The readers (qurra') differed concerning the recitation of this. Some of them recited ﴿فِي ظُلَلٍ﴾ (fi zulal), meaning the plural of ẓullah (a canopy), just as ḥullah (a garment) is pluralized as ḥullal. Others recited ﴿في ظِلالٍ﴾ (fi ẓilal). * *

As for His saying ﴿reclining upon couches﴾:

The arā'ik (couches) are the canopied beds (ḥijāl) in which there are thrones (surur) and mattresses (furush). Its singular is arīkah. Some of them claimed that every bed is an arīkah, and he cited for his claim the verse of Dhu al-Rummah:

.......................... as if they were touching with the ma'zā'... the touch of the arā'ik [[This is part of a verse by Dhu al-Rummah (his Diwan, 422), whose first half is:

"khuddan jafat fi al-sayr hatta ka'annama" — and khuddan is an object governed by kasa in the preceding verse. The commentator of his Diwan said: they meant "they clothed [the place] where the winds blew out the cheeks..." etc., i.e., they made the place where they slept a covering for the cheeks. End of quote. The ma'zā' is land containing stones and pebbles. The arā'ik: its singular is arīkah, which is a bed within a canopy. He says: from the intensity of sleep they see stony ground as like bedding on couches. Abu 'Ubaydah cited the verse in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 207) at the saying of the Exalted, (on the arā'ik), and said: its singular is arīkah, which is bedding within canopies. Dhu al-Rummah said: "khuddan ..." the verse, making it a bed.]]

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿reclining upon couches﴾, he said: they are the thrones within canopies.

⁕ Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿reclining upon couches﴾, he said: the arā'ik are thrones upon which are canopies.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿reclining therein upon couches﴾, he said: the arā'ik are thrones within canopies.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿upon couches﴾, he said: thrones upon which are canopies.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, who said: Muhammad claimed that 'Ikrimah said: the arā'ik are thrones within canopies.

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan, and a man asked him about the arā'ik, and he said: they are the canopies. The people of Yemen say: "arīkat fulan" (so-and-so's couch). And I heard 'Ikrimah, when asked about them, say: they are canopies upon thrones.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿upon couches﴾, he said: they are canopies in which are thrones.

* *

As for His saying ﴿For them therein is fruit﴾:

He says: for those whom He mentioned, may He be blessed and exalted, among the people of Paradise, in Paradise, there is fruit, ﴿and for them is whatever they request﴾, meaning: for them therein is whatever they wish for. It has been mentioned from the Arabs that they say: "da' 'alayya ma shi'ta" (ask of me whatever you wish), i.e., wish of me whatever you want.

* *

As for His saying ﴿[They will have] peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾:

Concerning the nominative case of salamun there are two possibilities according to the view of some of the Kufan grammarians. The first: that it is the predicate of mā yaddda'ūn, so the meaning of the speech is: "for them is whatever they request, granted to them, pure." When the meaning of the speech is directed to this, the word qawl (word) is then in the accusative as an emphatic element outside of the salām, as if it were said: "for them therein is whatever they request, granted, pure, truly," as if it were said: "He said it as a saying." The second possibility: that His saying salamun is in the nominative by way of praise, meaning: "it is peace for them, a word from God." It has been mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is ﴿salaman qawlan﴾, on the basis that the statement ends at His saying ﴿and for them is whatever they request﴾, then salaman is put in the accusative for emphasis, meaning: "granting peace, a word." Some of the grammarians of Basra said: qawlan is in the accusative as a substitute for the verb's wording, as if he said: "I say that as a saying." He said: whoever puts it in the accusative places it as the predicate of the definite in His saying ﴿and for them﴾ therein ﴿is whatever they request﴾.

What is more correct in accordance with what has come in the report from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi is that salamun should be the predicate of His saying ﴿and for them is whatever they request﴾, so the meaning would be: for them therein is whatever they request, and that is peace from God upon them, meaning: a greeting from God, and qawlan would be an explanation of "what they request," and the word qawl would be outside of His saying "salam."

I only said that this is more correct because of what Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri related to us, from Harmalah, from Sulayman ibn Humayd, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b narrating to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, saying: When God has finished with the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire, He will come walking in canopies of clouds with the angels, and He will stop at the first people of a rank, and greet them, and they will return the greeting to Him. And it is in the Qur'an: ﴿peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾. Then He will say: "Ask." They will say: "We ask nothing, by Your might and majesty, that if You were to divide among us the provisions of the two weighty ones (jinn and humankind), we would feed them, give them drink, and clothe them." He will say: "Ask." They will say: "We ask Your pleasure." He will say: "My pleasure has settled you in the abode of My honor." He does this with the people of each rank until He reaches the last. He said: "If a woman of the dark-eyed houris appeared, the light of her two bracelets would extinguish the sun and the moon, so how about the one adorned with them?"

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Harmalah related to us, from Sulayman ibn Humayd, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrating to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: When God has finished with the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire, He will come in canopies of clouds and the angels, and He will greet the people of Paradise, and they will return the greeting. Al-Qurazi said: And this is in the Book of God: ﴿peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾? Then He will say: "Ask Me." They will say: "What shall we ask of You, O Lord?" He will say: "Rather, ask Me." They will say: "We ask You, O Lord, for Your pleasure." He will say: "My pleasure has settled you in the abode of My honor." They will say: "O Lord, and what is it that we ask of You? By Your might, Your majesty, and the loftiness of Your station, if You were to divide among us the provision of the two weighty ones, we would feed them, give them drink, clothe them, and serve them, and that would not diminish us at all." He will say: "Indeed, with Me is more." He will do this for them in their ranks until He sits upon His seat. Then gifts from God will come to them, carried to them by the angels. Then he mentioned the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: Abu 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Harmalah related to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Humayd related to us, that he heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi narrating to 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: When God has finished with the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire, He will come walking in canopies of clouds and stop. He said: then he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: They will say: "What then shall we ask of You, O Lord? By Your might, Your majesty, and the loftiness of Your station, if You were to divide among us the provisions of the two weighty ones, jinn and humankind, we would feed them, give them drink, and serve them, without that diminishing anything of what we have." He will say: "Yes, so ask Me." They will say: "We ask Your pleasure." He will say: "My pleasure has settled you in the abode of My honor." He does this with the people of each rank until He reaches His assembly. The rest of the report is similar to it. So this saying which Muhammad ibn Ka'b said indicates that "salam" is an explanation of His saying ﴿what they request﴾, and that the word qawl is outside of salam.

* *

As for His saying ﴿from a Lord Most Merciful﴾:

Meaning: Merciful toward them, in that He did not punish them for the sins they committed in the world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 56–58:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿They and their spouses are in shade, reclining upon couches﴾ (56) ﴿For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they request﴾ (57) ﴿[They will have] peace, a word from a Lord Most Merciful﴾ (58).

By His saying ﴿They﴾, He, may He be exalted, means the people of Paradise, ﴿and their spouses﴾ among the people of Paradise, in Paradise.

As [was transmitted]:

⁕ Al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Waqqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿They and their spouses are in shade﴾, he said: "their wives, in shades (zilal)."

The readers (qurra') differed concerning the recitation of this. Some of them recited ﴿فِي ظُلَلٍ﴾ (fi zulal), meaning the plural of ẓullah (a canopy), just as ḥullah (a garment) is pluralized as ḥullal. Others recited ﴿في ظِلالٍ﴾ (fi ẓilal). When it is recited thus, it has two possible meanings: The first is that it means the plural of ẓulal, which signifies a shelter (kinn), so the sense of the word then is: they and their spouses are in shelter, not exposed to the sun as the people of this world are exposed to it, because there is no sun there. The second is that it means the plural of ẓullah, and its plural form is comparable to their plural of khullah (a friend) in abundance: khilal, and of qullah (a jar): qilal.

* *

As for His saying ﴿reclining upon couches﴾:

The arā'ik (couches) are the canopied beds (ḥijāl) in which there are thrones (surur) and mattresses (furush). Its singular is arīkah. Some of them claimed that every bed is an arīkah, and he cited for his claim the verse of Dhu al-Rummah:

.......................... as if they were touching with the ma'zā'... the touch of the arā'ik [[This is part of a verse by Dhu al-Rummah (his Diwan, 422), whose first half is:

"khuddan jafat fi al-sayr hatta ka'annama" — and khuddan is an object governed by kasa in the preceding verse. The commentator of his Diwan said: they meant "they clothed [the place] where the winds blew out the cheeks..." etc., i.e., they made the place where they slept a covering for the cheeks. End of quote. The ma'zā' is land containing stones and pebbles. The arā'ik: its singular is arīkah, which is a bed within a canopy. He says: from the intensity of sleep they see stony ground as like bedding on couches. Abu 'Ubaydah cited the verse in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 207) at the saying of the Exalted, (on the arā'ik), and said: its singular is arīkah, which is bedding within canopies. Dhu al-Rummah said: "khuddan ..." the verse, making it a bed.]]

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿reclining upon couches﴾, he said: they are the thrones within canopies.

⁕ Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God ﴿reclining upon couches﴾, he said: the arā'ik are thrones upon which are canopies.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn related to us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿reclining therein upon couches﴾, he said: the arā'ik are thrones within canopies.

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿upon couches﴾, he said: thrones upon which are canopies.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, who said: Muhammad claimed that 'Ikrimah said: the arā'ik are thrones within canopies.

The people of Yemen say: "arīkat fulan" (so-and-so's couch). And I heard 'Ikrimah, when asked about them, say: they are canopies upon thrones.

It has been mentioned from the Arabs that they say: "da' 'alayya ma shi'ta" (ask of me whatever you wish), i.e., wish of me whatever you want.

Concerning the nominative case of salamun there are two possibilities according to the view of some of the Kufan grammarians. The first: that it is the predicate of mā yaddda'ūn, so the meaning of the speech is: "for them is whatever they request, granted to them, pure." When the meaning of the speech is directed to this, the word qawl (word) is then in the accusative as an emphatic element outside of the salām, as if it were said: "for them therein is whatever they request, granted, pure, truly," as if it were said: "He said it as a saying." The second possibility: that His saying salamun is in the nominative by way of praise, meaning: "it is peace for them, a word from God." It has been mentioned that in the reading of 'Abd Allah it is ﴿salaman qawlan﴾, on the basis that the statement ends at His saying ﴿and for them is whatever they request﴾, then salaman is put in the accusative for emphasis, meaning: "granting peace, a word." Some of the grammarians of Basra said: qawlan is in the accusative as a substitute for the verb's wording, as if he said: "I say that as a saying." The interpretation of His words, ﴿And withdraw yourselves today, O you criminals﴾ (59)

By His words ﴿withdraw yourselves﴾ (wa-mtāzū) is meant: separate yourselves. It is of the form ifta'alū, from māza yamīzu (to distinguish, to separate), whose verbal form is imtāza yamtāzu imtiyāzan.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wīl) have said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said so:

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words ﴿And withdraw yourselves today, O you criminals﴾, he said: They will be removed from every good.

• Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahmān ibn Muhammad al-Muhāribī narrated to us, from Ismā'īl ibn Rāfi', from one who narrated to him, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazī, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will command Hell, and a bright, dark neck will emerge from it, and then He will say: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan﴾ ... the verse, until His words ﴿This is Hell which you were promised﴾ ﴿And withdraw yourselves today, O you criminals﴾. Then the people will be separated and will kneel down." This is the meaning of Allah's words ﴿And you will see every nation﴾ ... the verse.

So the meaning of the speech is: And separate yourselves today from the believers, O you who disbelieve in Allah, for you are coming to a place other than theirs, and entering other than their entrance.

As for His words ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾, there is in the speech an omitted element that is understood from the context, and it is: Then it will be said: Did I not charge you, O children of Adam? He says: Did I not enjoin and command you in the world that you should not worship Satan, so that you obey him in disobedience to Allah? ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾: He says, and I say to you: Indeed Satan is to you a clear enemy, who has made his enmity manifest by his refusal to prostrate to your father Adam, out of envy of him for the honour Allah had given him, and by his deception of him, until he expelled him and his wife from the Garden.

He says: Did I not charge you that you should worship Me alone, apart from everything else worshipped as gods and rivals, and obey Me alone? For sincere worship of Me, devoting obedience to Me, and disobeying Satan, is the correct religion and the straight path.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 36, verses 62–64:

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he had led astray from among you a great multitude. Then did you not use reason?﴾ (62) ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised.﴾ (63) ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to deny.﴾ (64)

Exalted is He, by His saying ﴿Indeed, he had led astray from among you a great multitude﴾, means: Indeed, Satan had turned away from My obedience and from My singling out of divinity a great number of you, until they worshipped him and took gods other than Me to worship.

As related to us:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, he had led astray from among you a great multitude﴾, who said: "Khalqan" (a great multitude, creation).

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this word. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufans recite ﴿jibilan﴾ with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam. Some of the Meccans and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recite it as ﴿jubulan﴾ with a damma on the jim and the ba, and a light lam. Some of the reciters of Basra recite it as ﴿jubulan﴾ with a damma on the jim and a sukun on the ba. All of these are well-known dialectal forms. However, I do not prefer any recitation except one of the two: the first, with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam, or the second, with a damma on the jim and the ba and a light lam, because these are the recitations upon which the majority of the reciters of the major cities agree.

His saying ﴿Then did you not use reason?﴾

It means: Then did you not use reason, O polytheists, when you obeyed Satan in worshipping other than God, that you should not obey your enemy and the enemy of God and worship other than God?

His saying ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised.﴾

It means: This is Hell with which you were threatened in the world for your disbelief in God and your denial of His messengers, so you used to deny it. It has been said that Hell is the first of the gates of the Fire.

His saying ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to deny.﴾

It means: Burn in it today and enter it. By "today" is meant the Day of Resurrection. ﴿For what you used to deny﴾: that is, for what you used to reject in the world and deny.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, he had led astray from among you a great multitude﴾, who said: "Khalqan" (a great multitude, creation).

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this word. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufans recite ﴿jibilan﴾ with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam. Some of the Meccans and the majority of the reciters of Kufa recite it as ﴿jubulan﴾ with a damma on the jim and the ba, and a light lam. Some of the reciters of Basra recite it as ﴿jubulan﴾ with a damma on the jim and a sukun on the ba. All of these are well-known dialectal forms. However, I do not prefer any recitation except one of the two: the first, with a kasra on the jim and a shaddah on the lam, or the second, with a damma on the jim and the ba and a light lam, because these are the recitations upon which the majority of the reciters of the major cities agree.

His saying ﴿Then did you not use reason?﴾

It means: Then did you not use reason, O polytheists, when you obeyed Satan in worshipping other than God, that you should not obey your enemy and the enemy of God and worship other than God?

His saying ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised.﴾

It means: This is Hell with which you were threatened in the world for your disbelief in God and your denial of His messengers, so you used to deny it. It has been said that Hell is the first of the gates of the Fire.

His saying ﴿Burn therein today for what you used to deny.﴾

It means: Burn in it today and enter it. By "today" is meant the Day of Resurrection. ﴿For what you used to deny﴾: that is, for what you used to reject in the world and deny.

The meaning of His words, *"Today We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn"* (36:65):

He, may He be exalted, means by His words, ﴿Today We will seal their mouths﴾: today We will stamp upon the mouths of the polytheists. That is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And their hands will speak to Us﴾ concerning what they did in the world of the disobedience of God. ﴿And their feet will bear witness﴾. It has been said that what speaks from their feet is their thighs, from the left leg. ﴿To what they used to earn﴾ in the world of sins.

Commentators of the ta'wil (the explanation and interpretation of the Qur'an) have said things similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

It was narrated to me by Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, who said: Yunus ibn Ubayd related to us, from Humayd ibn Hilal, who said: Abu Burdah said: Abu Musa said: The believer will be summoned to account on the Day of Resurrection, and his Lord will present to him his deed, between Him and him. He will confess and say: "Yes, my Lord, I did, I did, I did." Then God will forgive him his sins and conceal them from him, so no creature on earth will see any of those sins, and his good deeds will appear, and he will wish that all people could see them. The disbeliever and the hypocrite will be summoned to account, and his Lord will present to him his deed, and he will deny it and say: "O Lord, by Your might, these recording angels have written down for me what I did not do." The angel will say to him: "Did you not do such and such on such a day at such a place?" He will say: "No, by Your might, my Lord, I did not do it." When he does this, his mouth will be sealed. Al-Ash'ari said: I think the first thing that will speak from him will be his right thigh. Then he recited: ﴿Today We will seal their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn﴾.

It was narrated to us by Abu Kurayb, who said: Yahya related to me, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, from al-A'mash, from al-Sha'bi, who said: It will be said to a man on the Day of Resurrection: "You did such and such." He will say: "I did not do it." Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak. He will say to his limbs: "May God curse you, I was only arguing for your sake."

It was narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning his words ﴿Today We will seal their mouths﴾ ... the verse. He said: There had been disputes and speech, and this was its end: ﴿We will seal their mouths﴾.

It was narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Awf al-Ta'i, who said: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Ibn Ayyash, from Dhamdham ibn Zur'ah, from Shurayh ibn Ubayd, from Uqbah ibn Amir, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The first thing of a person to speak will be his thigh, from his left leg, on the day when God seals the mouths."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 66–67:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race for the path; then how could they see?﴾ (36:66)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race for the path﴾. Some of them said: the meaning of that is: "And if We willed, We would have blinded them to guidance, and misguided them from the straight course (al-mahajjah)."

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes﴾, he says: "I would have misguided them and blinded them to guidance."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "And if We willed, We would have left them blind."

Those who said that:

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race for the path; then how could they see?﴾ He said: "If He willed, He would have obliterated their eyes and left them blind, wandering about."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying (And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes, so they would race for the path; then how could they see?) He says: "If We willed, We would have left them blind, wandering about."

And this saying which we have mentioned from al-Hasan and Qatadah is more fitting to the interpretation of the speech, because God only threatened with it a disbelieving people. So there is no sense in saying, "And they are disbelievers, if We willed, We would have misguided them," when He has already misguided them. Rather He said: If We willed, We would punish them for their disbelief, so We would obliterate their eyes and make them blind, unable to see a path or be guided to it. The obliterating (al-tams) of the eye is that there is no slit (gharr) between the two eyelids, and that is the split between the two lids [[Thus in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah (photographic copy of al-Jami'ah, folio 207).]], as the wind obliterates a trace. It is said: a blind man who is obliterated (a'ma matmus) and tamis.

* *

And His saying ﴿so they would race for the path﴾

He says: so they would hasten to the road.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿so they would race for the path﴾: "The road."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿so they would race for the path﴾, i.e., the road.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿so they would race for the path﴾: "The path (al-sirat) is the road."

* *

And His saying ﴿then how could they see?﴾

He says: by what way could they see to travel among the roads, when We have obliterated their eyes.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us... from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿then how could they see?﴾: "And We have obliterated their eyes."

Those who directed the interpretation of His saying ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes﴾ to mean blindness to guidance also directed the interpretation of His saying ﴿then how could they see?﴾ to mean: then how could they be guided to the truth?

Those who said that:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿then how could they see?﴾ He says: "How could they be guided?"

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿then how could they see?﴾ He says: "They would not see the truth."

* *

And His saying ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And if We willed, We would have made these polytheists sit on their feet in their dwellings, ﴿so they would not be able to proceed forward, nor return backward﴾. He says: they would not be able to go forward in front of them, nor to return behind them.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of that. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Uliyyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan: ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places﴾ He said: "If We willed, We would have made them sit."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places﴾, i.e., We would have made them sit on their feet ﴿so they would not be able to proceed forward, nor return backward﴾, so they could neither advance nor retreat.

Others said: rather the meaning of that is: And if We willed, We would have destroyed them in their dwellings.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And if We willed, We would have transformed them in their places, so they would not be able to proceed forward, nor return backward﴾: He says: "If We willed, We would have destroyed them in their homes, and al-makanah and al-makan have the same meaning. We have already explained that earlier."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 68–70:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Then will they not reason?﴾ (68) ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a reminder and a clear Qur'an,﴾ (69) ﴿to warn whoever is alive and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾ (70)

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: ﴿And whomever We grant long life﴾ – that is, We extend his lifespan – ﴿We reverse him in creation﴾ – We return him to a state like his condition in youth, of decrepitude and old age. This is the reversal in creation, so that he comes to know nothing after the knowledge he used to have.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation﴾, he said: Whomever We extend in life, We reverse in creation, so that he does not know anything after knowledge, meaning senility (al-haram).

The readers differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿nunakkisuhu﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited it as ﴿nankisuhu﴾ with a fatha on the first nun and a sukun on the second. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as ﴿nunakkisuhu﴾ with a damma on the first nun, a fatha on the second, and a shaddah on the kaf.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations among the readers of the regions; whichever of them a reciter uses is correct. However, the recitation followed by the majority of the Kufan readers is more pleasing to me, because the reversal by Allah in creation is a state after a state and a thing after a thing, and so the shaddah supports it.

Likewise they differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿afalā ya'qilūn﴾. The readers of Medina recited it ﴿afalā ta'qilūn﴾ with the ta', in the form of direct address. The readers of Kufa recited it with the ya', as a report. Reciting it with the ya' is more akin to the apparent sense of the revelation, because it is an argument from Allah against the polytheists about whom He said ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes﴾. Presenting it as a report, in the manner of His saying ﴿We would have obliterated their eyes﴾, is more pleasing to me, although the other reading is not rejected.

By His saying ﴿Then will they not reason?﴾, the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned, means: Will these polytheists not reason the power of Allah over what He wills, by their witnessing what they witness of His directing His creation as He wills and loves, from youth to old age, and from reversal after old age into decrepitude?

* *

And His saying ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: We did not teach Muhammad poetry, nor is it befitting for him to be a poet.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾, he said: It was said to 'A'ishah: Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) quote anything of poetry? She said: It was the most hateful speech to him, except that he would quote a line of the brother of the Banu Qays, reversing its last part to be its first and its first to be its last. Abu Bakr said to him: It is not like this. The Prophet of Allah said: "Indeed, by Allah, I am not a poet, nor is it befitting for me."

* *

And His saying ﴿It is not but a reminder﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: It is nothing but a reminder – by His saying "it" (huwa), meaning Muhammad, is nothing but a reminder to you, O people, Allah reminding you by sending him to you and alerting you through him to your portion. ﴿And a clear Qur'an﴾ – says: And this which Muhammad has brought you is a clear Qur'an, meaning it becomes clear to whoever reflects upon it with intellect and understanding, that it is a revelation from Allah sent down to Muhammad, and that it is not poetry nor the speech of a soothsayer.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And a clear Qur'an﴾, he said: This is the Qur'an.

* *

And His saying ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾

Says: Muhammad is nothing but a reminder to you, so that he may warn whoever among you, O people, is alive – alive of heart, understanding what is said to him and grasping what is made clear to him, not dead of heart and dull.

According to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from a man, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾, he said: Whoever is intelligent.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾: alive of heart, alive of sight.

* *

His saying ﴿and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers﴾

Says: And the punishment is made due upon the people of disbelief in Allah, those who turn away from following Him and who oppose what has come to them from Allah.

According to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers﴾: by their deeds.

His saying ﴿and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers﴾

Says: And the punishment is made due upon the people of disbelief in Allah, those who turn away from following Him and who oppose what has come to them from Allah.

According to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers﴾: by their deeds.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 68–70:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Then will they not reason?﴾ (68) ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a reminder and a clear Qur'an,﴾ (69) ﴿to warn whoever is alive and that the word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers.﴾ (70)

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: ﴿And whomever We grant long life﴾ – that is, We extend his lifespan – ﴿We reverse him in creation﴾ – We return him to a state like his condition in youth, of decrepitude and old age. This is the reversal in creation, so that he comes to know nothing after the knowledge he used to have.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation﴾, he said: Whomever We extend in life, We reverse in creation, so that he does not know anything after knowledge, meaning senility (al-haram).

The readers differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿nunakkisuhu﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited it as ﴿nankisuhu﴾ with a fatha on the first nun and a sukun on the second. The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it as ﴿nunakkisuhu﴾ with a damma on the first nun, a fatha on the second, and a shaddah on the kaf.

The correct view on this is that both are well-known recitations among the readers of the regions; whichever of them a reciter uses is correct. However, the recitation followed by the majority of the Kufan readers is more pleasing to me, because the reversal by Allah in creation is a state after a state and a thing after a thing, and so the shaddah supports it.

Likewise they differed in the recitation of His saying ﴿afalā ya'qilūn﴾. The readers of Medina recited it ﴿afalā ta'qilūn﴾ with the ta', in the form of direct address. The readers of Kufa recited it with the ya', as a report. Reciting it with the ya' is more akin to the apparent sense of the revelation, because it is an argument from Allah against the polytheists about whom He said ﴿And if We willed, We would have obliterated their eyes﴾. Presenting it as a report, in the manner of His saying ﴿We would have obliterated their eyes﴾, is more pleasing to me, although the other reading is not rejected.

By His saying ﴿Then will they not reason?﴾, the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned, means: Will these polytheists not reason the power of Allah over what He wills, by their witnessing what they witness of His directing His creation as He wills and loves, from youth to old age, and from reversal after old age into decrepitude?

* *

And His saying ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: We did not teach Muhammad poetry, nor is it befitting for him to be a poet.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for him﴾, he said: It was said to 'A'ishah: Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) quote anything of poetry? She said: It was the most hateful speech to him, except that he would quote a line of the brother of the Banu Qays, reversing its last part to be its first and its first to be its last. Abu Bakr said to him: It is not like this. The Prophet of Allah said: "Indeed, by Allah, I am not a poet, nor is it befitting for me."

* *

And His saying ﴿It is not but a reminder﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be mentioned: It is nothing but a reminder – by His saying "it" (huwa), meaning Muhammad, is nothing but a reminder to you, O people, Allah reminding you by sending him to you and alerting you through him to your portion. ﴿And a clear Qur'an﴾ – says: And this which Muhammad has brought you is a clear Qur'an, meaning it becomes clear to whoever reflects upon it with intellect and understanding, that it is a revelation from Allah sent down to Muhammad, and that it is not poetry nor the speech of a soothsayer.

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And a clear Qur'an﴾, he said: This is the Qur'an.

* *

And His saying ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾

Says: Muhammad is nothing but a reminder to you, so that he may warn whoever among you, O people, is alive – alive of heart, understanding what is said to him and grasping what is made clear to him, not dead of heart and dull.

According to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from a man, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾, he said: Whoever is intelligent.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿to warn whoever is alive﴾: alive of heart, alive of sight.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: "Have they not seen that We created for them, of what Our hands have made, cattle, so that they are their owners? (71) And We have subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and of some of them they eat." (72)

Say: His words, may He be remembered, "Have they not seen" — these polytheists who associate with Allah the gods and idols — "that We created for them of what Our hands have made" — meaning: of what We created of creatures — "cattle," which are the livestock that Allah created for the children of Adam and subjected to them, of camels, cattle and sheep — "so they are their owners" — meaning: they manage them as they wish, by their dominance over them and their control.

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "so they are their owners": i.e., those who control them.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "Have they not seen that We created for them of what Our hands have made, cattle, so that they are their owners." He was asked: "Are these the camels?" He said: "Yes." He said: "And cattle are among the cattle (an'am), but they are not included in this verse." He said: "The camels, cattle and sheep are the cattle (an'am)," and he recited "eight pairs" (Qur'an 6:143). He said: "Cattle and camels are the ni'am (livestock), and sheep do not enter into the ni'am."

* * *

And His words "And We have subjected them to them,"

Meaning: We subjected these cattle to them, "so some of them they ride" — meaning: some of them they ride, such as camels on which they travel; it is said, "this is a riding animal (dabbat rukub)," and "rukub" with a damma is the act of riding — "and of some of them they eat," their flesh.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said what we have said regarding this.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 73–74:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And for them therein are benefits and drinks; will they not then be grateful?﴾ (73) ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah, that perhaps they might be helped.﴾ (74)

The Exalted says: And for them in these livestock are benefits, namely benefits in their wool, their fur and their hair, by their making from these furnishings and goods, and from their hides shelters, and drinks, which they drink from their milk.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And for them therein are benefits﴾: they wear their wool; ﴿and drinks﴾: they drink their milk.

* *

As for His saying ﴿will they not then be grateful?﴾

He says: Will they not be grateful for this blessing of Mine and My kindness to them by obeying Me, affirming divinity and worship for Me alone, and abandoning obedience to Satan and the worship of idols?

* *

As for His saying ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah﴾

He says: These polytheists have taken gods besides Allah to worship, ﴿that perhaps they might be helped﴾, meaning: hoping that those gods would help them against the punishment and chastisement of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 73–74:

The commentary on His words, exalted is He: ﴿They are not able to help them, and they are a host brought up before them (for punishment)﴾ (75)

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be great: These idols are not able to help them against God if He intends harm for them, nor can they repel any harm from them.

* *

And His words ﴿and they are a host brought up before them﴾

That is: these polytheists are a host brought up for their gods.

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of His words ﴿muhdarun﴾ (brought up), and where their "bringing" to them takes place. Some said: by this is meant, "and they are a host brought up for them at the reckoning."

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿and they are a host brought up for them﴾, he said: "at the reckoning."

And others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "and they are a host brought up for them in this world, who become angry on their behalf."

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿they are not able to help them﴾ (the gods) ﴿and they are a host brought up for them﴾: "The polytheists become angry for the gods in this world, while they (the gods) do not bring them any good nor repel any evil from them; they are only idols."

What Qatadah said is, in our view, the more correct of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of this, because on the reckoning the idols will disown those who worshipped them and what they worshipped, so how could they then be a host for them? Rather, in this world they are a host for them, who become angry on their behalf and fight in their defence.

And His words, exalted is He, ﴿So let not their speech grieve you﴾: says the Exalted, may His remembrance be great, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So let not the speech of these polytheists from your people grieve you, O Muhammad, when they say to you: "You are a poet, and what you have brought us is not poetry," nor their denial of the signs of God and their rejection of your prophethood.

* *

And His words ﴿We know what they conceal and what they reveal﴾

Says the Exalted, may His remembrance be great: We know that what prompts them to say that is envy, and they know that what you have brought them is not poetry, nor does it resemble poetry, and that you are not a liar; so We know what they conceal of their recognition of the truth of what you call them to, and what they reveal of their denial of that openly with their tongues.
