Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 77–79:

Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen, and yet he is an open adversary?﴾ ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Has man not considered that We created him﴾. Scholars differed regarding the man intended by His words ﴿Has man not considered﴾. Some said: it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

Mention of those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾: Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a bone.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And he presents to Us an example﴾: Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾: It was related to us that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, crumbled it, then scattered it in the wind, and then said: "O Muhammad, who will give life to this when it is decayed?" He said: "Allah will give it life, then cause you to die, then cause you to enter the Fire." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed him on the day of Uhud.

Others said: rather, it refers to al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

Mention of those who said so:

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, crumbled it before him, and said: "O Muhammad, will Allah resurrect this alive after it has rotted?" He said: "Yes, Allah will resurrect this, then cause you to die, then give you life, then cause you to enter the Hellfire." He said: And the verses were revealed: ﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen, and yet he is an open adversary?﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

Others said: rather, it refers to Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

Mention of those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen﴾ ... to His words ﴿and it is decayed﴾: Abdullah ibn Ubayy came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, broke it with his hand, and said: "O Muhammad, how will Allah resurrect this when it is decayed?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will resurrect this, and cause you to die, then cause you to enter Jahannam." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾

So the meaning of the statement is: Has this man who says ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ not considered that We created him from a drop of semen, then made him into a proper, well-formed creature? ﴿And yet he is an open adversary﴾: that is, he is one who disputes with his Lord, contesting what his Lord told him, that He is going to make His creatures live again after their death. He says: "Who will give life to these bones when they are decayed?", denying Allah's power to give them life.

* *

His words ﴿open﴾:

That is, he makes his dispute and his saying plain to whoever hears it, that he is disputing with his Lord who created him.

* *

His words ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation﴾:

That is, he presents to Us a likeness through his saying ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾, since no one is able to give life to such things. That is, He has made us like one who cannot give life to such creatures. ﴿And forgets his own creation﴾: that is, he forgets Our creating him, how We created him, and that he was nothing but a drop, until We made him a well-formed, speaking creature. That is, he does not reflect on Our creating him, so that he would know that the One who created him from a drop until he became a human, well-formed, speaking, and active, is not unable to restore the dead to life, and to restore the decayed bones to the form they had before perishing. Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾ to this polytheist who says to you: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?": ﴿He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾, that is, He will give them life who originated their creation the first time when they were nothing. ﴿And He is Knowing of every creation﴾, that is, He possesses knowledge of all His creation, of how to cause death, how to give life, how to originate, and how to restore, nothing of the affair of His creation being hidden from Him.

His words ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation﴾:

That is, he presents to Us a likeness through his saying ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾, since no one is able to give life to such things. That is, He has made us like one who cannot give life to such creatures. ﴿And forgets his own creation﴾: that is, he forgets Our creating him, how We created him, and that he was nothing but a drop, until We made him a well-formed, speaking creature. That is, he does not reflect on Our creating him, so that he would know that the One who created him from a drop until he became a human, well-formed, speaking, and active, is not unable to restore the dead to life, and to restore the decayed bones to the form they had before perishing. Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾ to this polytheist who says to you: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?": ﴿He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾, that is, He will give them life who originated their creation the first time when they were nothing. ﴿And He is Knowing of every creation﴾, that is, He possesses knowledge of all His creation, of how to cause death, how to give life, how to originate, and how to restore, nothing of the affair of His creation being hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verse 77–79:

Concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen, and yet he is an open adversary?﴾ ﴿And he presents to Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾ ﴿Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿Has man not considered that We created him﴾. Scholars differed regarding the man intended by His words ﴿Has man not considered﴾. Some said: it refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

Mention of those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Umarah narrated to me, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾: Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a bone.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And he presents to Us an example﴾: Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿He says: "Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?"﴾: It was related to us that Ubayy ibn Khalaf came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, crumbled it, then scattered it in the wind, and then said: "O Muhammad, who will give life to this when it is decayed?" He said: "Allah will give it life, then cause you to die, then cause you to enter the Fire." He said: So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) killed him on the day of Uhud.

Others said: rather, it refers to al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.

Mention of those who said so:

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, crumbled it before him, and said: "O Muhammad, will Allah resurrect this alive after it has rotted?" He said: "Yes, Allah will resurrect this, then cause you to die, then give you life, then cause you to enter the Hellfire." He said: And the verses were revealed: ﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen, and yet he is an open adversary?﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

Others said: rather, it refers to Abdullah ibn Ubayy.

Mention of those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Has man not considered that We created him from a drop of semen﴾ ... to His words ﴿and it is decayed﴾: Abdullah ibn Ubayy came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with a decayed bone, broke it with his hand, and said: "O Muhammad, how will Allah resurrect this when it is decayed?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will resurrect this, and cause you to die, then cause you to enter Jahannam." So Allah revealed: ﴿Say: "He will give them life who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of every creation."﴾

So the meaning of the statement is: Has this man who says ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ not considered that We created him from a drop of semen, then made him into a proper, well-formed creature? ﴿And yet he is an open adversary﴾: that is, he is one who disputes with his Lord, contesting what his Lord told him, that He is going to make His creatures live again after their death. He says: "Who will give life to these bones when they are decayed?", denying Allah's power to give them life.

* *

His words ﴿open﴾:

That is, he makes his dispute and his saying plain to whoever hears it, that he is disputing with his Lord who created him.

* *

That is, he presents to Us a likeness through his saying ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾, since no one is able to give life to such things. That is, He has made us like one who cannot give life to such creatures. ﴿And forgets his own creation﴾: that is, he forgets Our creating him, how We created him, and that he was nothing but a drop, until We made him a well-formed, speaking creature. **The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿Who has made for you fire from the green tree, and then you kindle from it.﴾ (80) ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing.﴾ (81)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Say, "The One who brought them into being the first time will give them life," ﴿Who has made for you fire from the green tree﴾, meaning: He who brought forth for you fire from the green tree, which burns the tree. Nothing prevents Him from doing what He wills, and He is not incapable of giving life to the bones that have decayed, and returning them as perfect humans and a new creation, just as He originated them the first time.

Those who practise tafsir (exegesis) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Who has made for you fire from the green tree﴾, he said: He who brought forth this fire from this tree is able to resurrect it (the human).

* *

His saying ﴿and then you kindle from it﴾.

He says: and then you kindle fire from this tree. He said "minhu" (منه), and the pronoun (الهاء) refers to the tree, and He did not say "minha" (منها). The word "shajar" (الشجر) is a collective noun of "shajarah" (شجرة), because it took the form of "al-thamar" (الثمر) and "al-hasa" (الحصى), which are treated similarly. Had it been said "minha," it would also have been correct, because the Arabs treat such nouns as masculine at one time and feminine at another.

﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, alerting this disbeliever who said ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ to the error of his statement and the greatness of his ignorance: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens﴾, the seven of them, ﴿and the earth able to create﴾ the likes of you? For creating your likes from decayed bones is not greater than creating the heavens and the earth. He says: so how could He who is not incapable of creating what is greater than your creation find it impossible to give life to bones after they have decayed and crumbled?

His saying ﴿Yes, and He is the All-Creating, the All-Knowing﴾ means: Yes, He is able to create their likes, and He is the Creator of whatever He wills, the Doer of whatever He desires, the All-Knowing of everything He has created and will create, nothing hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 36, verses 82–83:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [36:82], and ﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things, and to Him you will be returned﴾ [36:83].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾ Qatadah used to say concerning this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, [He is], and He is the Knowing Creator﴾ [36:81], that he said: "This is an example of 'Indeed, His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is.'" He said: "There is nothing in the speech of the Arabs that is lighter or easier than that. So is the command of Allah."

* *

And His saying, ﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: So glorified is He who holds in His hand the dominion of everything and its treasuries.

* *

And His saying, ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾:

He says: And to Him you will return and go back after your deaths.

End of the commentary on Surah Ya-Sin.
